brief: The six-tool stack behind a one-person agency

slots.title: One person. Eleven clients. No team.
slots.sub: Six tools carry the work a small agency would hire four people to do. Here is each one and the job it actually replaced.

slots.title: Running solo fails at the seams
slots.body: The work is never what breaks you. What breaks you is the handoff between the work — the brief nobody wrote down, the invoice nobody sent, the follow-up nobody remembered.

slots.title: One home for every client
slots.body: Briefs, notes, SOPs and deliverables live in a single workspace. Nothing gets lost between a call and the work that follows it.

slots.title: Tasks move without drama
slots.body: Every request becomes a tracked item with an owner and a status. You always know what is next and what is blocked, without asking anyone.

slots.title: Faster than the idea gets cold
slots.body: Mockups and decks come out of components built once. Scope conversations happen over something real instead of a paragraph.

slots.title: Invoices that send themselves
slots.body: Contracts, deposits and reminders run on a schedule. The most awkward conversation in freelancing stops being a conversation.

slots.title: Next month is never a surprise
slots.body: Leads, proposals and renewals sit in one view. The quiet month you did not see coming is the one that ends a solo practice.

slots.headline: Tools do not make you an agency
slots.body: They remove the reasons one person cannot hold eleven clients. The work is still the work — this just stops the seams from failing.
